description: Naive French plural: append "s" from 2 upwards, unless the word already ends in "s". Real plural forms belong in Knowledge (set_ingredient_plural); until they exist all clients must be wrong in exactly the same way, which is what these vectors enforce.

cases.why: The baseline: exactly one stays singular, which is the same in French and English and so the case least likely to reveal a wrong port on its own.
French keeps the singular below 2, unlike English: "1,5 carotte".
The threshold is 2 and it is inclusive, so this is the first count that pluralises. Together with the 1.5 case it fixes the boundary exactly.
Reachable from describeQuantity: 160 g of carrot is 2.2 items.
Invariable words must not gain a second s ("ananass").
Fractions below one are singular too, so the rule is a single threshold at 2 rather than a special case for "exactly 1".
